claims.text: The initial cast alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and undergoes pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
Pack-cementation aluminizing will deposit a thin, aluminum-enriched surface layer on the alloy.
Aluminizing will enable a dense, adherent, and continuous Al2O3 scale to form on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Surface aluminum will preferentially oxidize to form stable alumina.
The alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The oxygen-diffusion barrier will prevent rapid oxidation and pesting.
Surface aluminizing will leave the bulk composition responsible for the alloy's mechanical properties substantially unaltered.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, aluminized specimens will have lower oxidation mass gain than untreated specimens.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, aluminized specimens will have thinner and more continuous oxide scales than untreated specimens.
Aluminized specimens will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility after oxidation exposure.
Aluminized specimens will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ after oxidation exposure.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr rapidly oxidizes and pests under comparable high-temperature air exposure.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr forms little or no protective oxide scale under comparable exposure.
The predicted oxidation benefit applies in air at temperatures up to 800 °C and exposure durations around 5 hours.
